paragraphs: Haringey Council approves and supports its own foster carers, and the independent agencies shown above also recruit in the borough. Fostering for the council means caring for Haringey's own children with its social workers behind you; an agency assesses, trains and supervises its own carers and takes children placed with it by councils, Haringey included. Since 1 October 2026 the council's recruitment has gone through the North London Fostering Hub, which Camden leads for Barnet, Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey and Islington. It builds on a partnership between the six councils that goes back to 2012, so first enquiries now go to Foster North London.

The council's fostering annual report for 2024/25 shows why it wants more local carers. On 31 March 2025 Haringey looked after 325 children, 235 of them in fostering homes; 136 children were with Haringey's own foster carers and 98 with independent agency carers. It had 109 approved fostering households, and 117 people enquired about fostering during the year. The report describes growing demand for homes for family groups, teenagers and children with complex needs, and names adolescents, large sibling groups and unaccompanied young people among those it most needs carers for. It has set a four-year marketing and recruitment plan to bring in a more diverse group of carers and rely less on agencies.

On support, the same report says Haringey relaunched its Mockingbird project with The Fostering Network and keeps regular support groups going, including one for male carers. The council's own pages promise help 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, specialist training and a supervising social worker, and say you do not need to be a parent yourself to foster, and that renting is fine as long as your housing is not temporary. Haringey offers short-term, long-term, parent and child, teenage and remand fostering, and supported lodgings for 16 to 21-year-olds.

The route to approval has five steps: a first conversation through Foster North London, a home visit, a compulsory three-day Skills to Foster course, an assessment with a social worker visiting at least weekly while checks are completed (up to four months), and the fostering panel. We do not yet have a Haringey allowance page, so ask the council and two or three of the agencies above for their current rates in writing. The Enfield, Barnet, Islington, Hackney and London pages list more services nearby.
